objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing thrombus formation and platelet adhesion in mechanical heart valves.
independent_variables: Nucleus (with nanostructured surface and hydrophilic polymers)
controls: Current mechanical heart valve without Nucleus
baseline: Current mechanical heart valve thrombus formation rate (± 20% standard deviation) and platelet adhesion rate (± 15% standard deviation)
procedure: In vitro testing with whole blood and platelet-rich plasma
30-day testing period for thrombus formation rate and 2-hour testing period for platelet adhesion rate
Histological analysis of explanted valves for thrombus formation rate and fluorescence microscopy for platelet adhesion rate
expected_result: A 30% reduction in thrombus formation rate and a 40% reduction in platelet adhesion rate compared to the current mechanical heart valve.
falsification_condition: No significant reduction in thrombus formation rate observed after 30 days of in vitro testing with whole blood and no significant reduction in platelet adhesion rate observed after 2 hours of in vitro testing with platelet-rich plasma.
sample_requirements: Mechanical heart valves with and without Nucleus, whole blood, platelet-rich plasma, and histological analysis equipment for thrombus formation rate and fluorescence microscopy equipment for platelet adhesion rate.
safety_constraints: Ensure proper handling and disposal of biological samples, and follow standard laboratory safety protocols.
estimated_duration: 12 months (including planning, testing, and data analysis)
information_gain: The effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing thrombus formation and platelet adhesion in mechanical heart valves, and the potential for future clinical trials to evaluate its safety and efficacy in patients.
